items.headline: Police NSF, 23, allegedly enters a female toilet at a training command and jumps from a building to evade arrest
items.summary: A 23-year-old police full-time national serviceman allegedly trespassed into a female toilet at the Police Training Command, then jumped from a building while trying to evade arrest, according to Mothership.

items.headline: Singapore to introduce laws in early 2027 to shield young social media users
items.summary: The Ministry of Digital Development and Information said it will introduce legislation early next year to strengthen safeguards for young social media users, focusing on age assurance and safer platform features.

items.headline: Petition against crow culling tops 2,500 signatures after officers filmed shooting birds near Aljunied
items.summary: A petition calling for an end to crow culling gathered more than 2,500 signatures - 2,573 as of Oct 21 - after National Parks Board officers were filmed shooting crows near Aljunied MRT station.

items.headline: Update: Singapore questions seven SGX-listed firms over possible links to the Indonesian haze fires
items.summary: Senior Minister K. Shanmugam said the government is questioning seven SGX-listed companies over possible links to the Indonesian fires driving transboundary haze, and that the exchange has also asked them about their operations. He warned Singapore would amend its laws urgently if needed to force cooperation.

items.headline: Update: Reliance's Jio Platforms is set for a record market debut on Wednesday
items.summary: Reliance's Jio Platforms is due to make its stock-market debut on Wednesday after its roughly US$108 billion offering - India's largest ever - drew heavy demand, with anchor bids topping US$26 billion from investors including BlackRock and GIC.

items.headline: Indian small-caps slump as margin calls bite and the Nifty extends its slide
items.summary: Indian small-cap stocks tumbled as leveraged investors faced margin calls, and the benchmark Nifty 50 fell for a fourth straight session, pressured by higher oil prices, Bloomberg reported.

items.headline: The rupee's Jio-fuelled rally fades as analysts warn of renewed pressure
items.summary: After climbing to a June high on foreign inflows into the Jio IPO, the rupee is expected to weaken again, with strategists pointing to elevated oil prices and foreign outflows as the IPO-driven support fades.

items.headline: Burnham backs tougher settlement rules and floats debating EU free movement, drawing a Brexit backlash
items.summary: Prime Minister Andy Burnham said he stands by the principle of Home Secretary Shabana Mahmood's immigration overhaul - replacing the five-year route to settlement with an 'earned settlement' system - and suggested debating a return to EU free movement, prompting Nigel Farage to call it a 'total betrayal of Brexit Britain'.

items.headline: Labour MPs warn Burnham's industrial-revival goals risk falling short
items.summary: A group of Labour MPs cautioned that Prime Minister Andy Burnham's pledge to re-industrialise Britain risks falling short without a shift in policy, Bloomberg reported, days before his government's first Budget.

items.headline: Healey set to raise UK bank taxes in Wednesday's Budget while ruling out a capital-gains hike
items.summary: Chancellor John Healey is expected to lean on higher bank taxes in the Oct 28 Budget - with reports the bank surcharge could rise to 8% from 3%, raising about GBP2 billion a year - while reportedly ruling out an increase in capital gains tax.

items.headline: UK bank shares slip and homebuilders rise as investors position for the Budget
items.summary: Shares in London-listed lenders have come under pressure on reports of a looming bank-tax raid, while homebuilders have gained on expectations of help for first-time buyers, as investors position for Chancellor Healey's first Budget.

items.headline: Israelis vote in an election that could end Netanyahu's long grip on power
items.summary: Israel holds its first election for all 120 Knesset seats since the October 2023 attacks, with polls pointing to a narrow edge for the opposition - averaging about 54 seats to roughly 49 for Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's bloc - but neither side clearly reaching the 61 needed to govern.

items.headline: Israeli strikes kill at least five people in Gaza, including a seven-year-old girl
items.summary: Israeli attacks killed at least five people in Gaza on Monday, among them a seven-year-old girl, with four reported dead in a strike on a displaced-persons camp in Khan Younis. Al Jazeera reported the toll since the October 2025 US-brokered truce has risen above 1,500.

items.headline: UN commission says Russia's attacks on Ukraine's energy grid amount to war crimes
items.summary: A UN Independent International Commission of Inquiry told the General Assembly that years of Russian strikes on Ukraine's power plants, grid and gas facilities since 2022 amount to war crimes, as both sides kept up daily attacks heading into winter.

items.headline: Britain sanctions 15 Sudanese commanders over atrocities a year after el-Fasher fell
items.summary: On the first anniversary of the Rapid Support Forces' capture of el-Fasher, the UK sanctioned 15 Sudanese military commanders, militia leaders and officials from both sides over alleged war crimes, including the use of sexual violence as a weapon.

items.headline: Bulgaria's presidential election heads to a run-off amid low turnout
items.summary: Bulgaria's presidential election will go to a run-off after no candidate won outright in a vote marked by low turnout, Al Jazeera reported.

items.headline: Update: Anthropic files for a record IPO, targeting a valuation of up to US$2 trillion
items.summary: Anthropic publicly filed its S-1 on Monday to list on Nasdaq under the ticker 'ANT', with a public debut expected in November. The maker of Claude reported US$16.3 billion in first-half revenue, up from about US$1.2 billion a year earlier; press reports put its target valuation at US$1.5 trillion to US$2 trillion.

items.headline: SpaceX locks in a US$40 billion chip-financing deal with Apollo for Nvidia's Vera Rubin GPUs
items.summary: SpaceX disclosed a binding commitment for about US$40 billion in AI-chip financing in a regulatory filing, under which an Apollo Global Management-managed entity will buy Nvidia's next-generation Vera Rubin chips and related hardware and lease the equipment back to SpaceX.

items.headline: Grok releases the first seven minutes of its AI-generated 'Odyssey' series
items.summary: xAI's Grok published the opening seven minutes of an AI-generated film it is calling Episode 1 of its 'Odyssey' series, its latest push into generative video.

items.headline: Recursive launches Flint, a laptop-sized coding model it says was largely built by AI
items.summary: AI startup Recursive released Flint, a coding model small enough to run on a laptop that it says was developed with heavy involvement from its own automated research system. The model is free to download on Hugging Face under an Apache 2.0 licence.

items.headline: Wall Street rebounds, led by chipmakers and Anthropic's IPO filing, as oil retreats
items.summary: US stocks rose on Monday, with gains led by chipmakers - a closely watched industry gauge climbed about 3.3% - and renewed AI optimism after Anthropic filed to go public, while oil eased, with Brent near US$115 and US crude around US$101 on hopes of calmer US-Iran tensions.

items.headline: EQT agrees to buy Range Resources in an all-stock deal valuing it above US$50 billion
items.summary: Natural-gas producer EQT agreed to acquire Range Resources in an all-stock deal valuing the company at more than US$50 billion, with completion expected in the first quarter of 2027; Range shares rose about 15%.

items.headline: Bon Secours Mercy Health to buy Surgery Partners for about US$5.7 billion, sending shares up 47%
items.summary: Surgery Partners jumped about 47% after Bon Secours Mercy Health agreed to acquire it for US$23.50 a share in cash, a deal valued at roughly US$5.7 billion.

items.headline: Whirlpool cuts its full-year revenue outlook to US$14.5 billion and misses estimates
items.summary: Whirlpool shares fell almost 9% after it trimmed full-year revenue guidance to US$14.5 billion from US$15 billion and missed third-quarter revenue estimates.

items.headline: JetBlue shares fall about 12% after a report its creditors hired a restructuring adviser
items.summary: JetBlue dropped about 12% following a Wall Street Journal report that its senior creditors had brought in a restructuring adviser; the carrier's stock is down roughly 50% so far this year.

items.headline: Antonelli can clinch his first F1 title at next weekend's Mexico City Grand Prix
items.summary: Kimi Antonelli leads the drivers' standings by 123 points over Mercedes team-mate George Russell with 125 still available. At the Mexico City Grand Prix on Oct 30-Nov 1 he need only avoid losing more than 23 points to Russell, or 24 to Lewis Hamilton, to become the youngest world champion in Formula 1 history.

items.headline: Zverev can seize the world No. 1 ranking with a deep run in Vienna
items.summary: Alexander Zverev, the top seed at the Vienna ATP 500 and 880 points behind Jannik Sinner, would overtake him to become world No. 1 on Nov 2 if he reaches the quarter-finals; Carlos Alcaraz is also in the draw for the first time since 2021.

items.headline: Rune ends his injury drought in Basel, surviving 32 aces from Halys
items.summary: Holger Rune claimed his first ATP Tour win since an Achilles injury, beating Quentin Halys 6-4, 6-7(2), 7-6(5) in the Swiss Indoors first round despite Halys serving 32 aces.

items.headline: Update: India chase a series-sealing win in Wellington as New Zealand rest Lockie Ferguson
items.summary: India, 2-0 up in the five-match series, play the third T20I against New Zealand in Wellington on Tuesday with a chance to seal it. New Zealand, who must win to stay alive, rested Lockie Ferguson and are without the injured Matt Henry, while India go in without Ishan Kishan.

items.headline: France reports the first known human infection with the livestock-borne Shamonda virus
items.summary: Scientists reported the first confirmed human case of Shamonda virus, a pathogen previously seen only in livestock, in a man in his sixties with cancer in France, who died on Oct 9. Researchers believe he was most likely infected by midge bites and say person-to-person spread is unlikely.

items.headline: Nearly half of reef-building coral species now face an elevated extinction risk
items.summary: A Nature study reassessing 892 reef-building coral species against the IUCN Red List found that 340 of the 774 species with enough data - about 44% - are now classed as threatened, with projected thermal stress the main driver.

items.headline: An AI trained on four million fossils suggests three 'big five' extinctions were gradual
items.summary: A machine-learning model trained on nearly four million fossil records suggests that three of Earth's 'big five' mass extinctions may have unfolded more gradually than long thought, researchers reported at a Geological Society of America meeting.

items.headline: A spectacular feathered-dinosaur fossil shows flight evolved more than once
items.summary: A stunningly preserved feathered-dinosaur fossil from China adds to evidence that birds and their closest relatives evolved the ability to fly several separate times, Nature reported.

fun_fact.headline: In a group of 23 people, two probably share a birthday
fun_fact.body: In a group of just 23 people, there is a better-than-even chance - about 50.7% - that two of them share a birthday, a result known as the birthday paradox. It feels wrong because we instinctively picture matching our own birthday, but what matters is the number of possible pairs: 23 people form 253 different pairs, enough to tip the odds past half. By 70 people, a shared birthday is all but certain, at over 99.9%.

puzzle.title: The Switch Room
puzzle.body: Outside a closed, windowless room are three identical on/off switches. Exactly one controls a single incandescent bulb inside; the other two do nothing. The door is shut, so you cannot see the bulb from outside. You may flip the switches as often as you like while the door is closed, but once you open the door you may not touch them again - and you get only one visit. How do you determine which switch controls the bulb?
puzzle.approach: You can gather information without seeing the bulb - think about what a light leaves behind even after it is switched off.
puzzle.answer: Turn switch 1 ON for several minutes, then turn it OFF, immediately turn switch 2 ON, and enter. If the bulb is lit, it is switch 2; if it is off but warm, it is switch 1 (heated filament); if off and cold, it is switch 3.

word_puzzle.title: Say It Another Way
word_puzzle.body: Each phrase is a perfect anagram of a single word or short phrase - rearrange all its letters: 1. DIRTY ROOM  2. THE EYES  3. A GENTLEMAN  4. ELEVEN PLUS TWO
word_puzzle.approach: Every letter is reused exactly once; the answer is often a playful description of the clue itself.
word_puzzle.answer: 1. DIRTY ROOM -> DORMITORY. 2. THE EYES -> THEY SEE. 3. A GENTLEMAN -> ELEGANT MAN. 4. ELEVEN PLUS TWO -> TWELVE PLUS ONE.
